items.title: Requested payment for 'Grundstücksregister' entry (offer, not a genuine debt)
items.computation: Letter dated 19.11.2026 states payment due by the printed calendar date 01.12.2026. 2026-12-01 is a Tuesday and not a public holiday in NRW, so no weekend/holiday shift applies. However, the letter's own small print says: 'Dieses Schreiben ist ein Angebot. Mit Ihrer Zahlung nehmen Sie es an; ein Vertrag kommt erst durch die Zahlung zustande.' This means no contract and no payment obligation currently exist — the document is an unsolicited commercial offer disguised as an invoice, and the 'entry' has nothing to do with the official Grundbuch. Therefore the stated due date is only the deadline printed on the offer, not a legally owed payment.

warnings: This is a known German scam/misleading-offer pattern: a private company styles an unsolicited commercial offer as an official-looking 'Rechnung' for a 'Grundstücksregister' entry that has no connection to the real, official Grundbuch (land registry) maintained by German courts.

The small print explicitly states 'Dieses Schreiben ist ein Angebot... ein Vertrag kommt erst durch die Zahlung zustande' — meaning no contract or debt exists yet; paying would voluntarily create a contract for a worthless private listing service.
Do not pay this invoice and do not send any bank details in response; if desired, this can be ignored or reported, as no real authority or court requires any action here.

The sender's address (Frankfurt am Main) and layout mimic an official registry notice, which is a hallmark of deceptive 'Gewerbeauskunft'-style invoicing scams targeting property/business owners in Germany.
